```{r, include=FALSE}
#----Variable manipulation-------###

ordered_osce <- c("P1FallBodySys_PhysExamScore","P1SprBates_PhysExamScore","P1SprBates_CommScore",
                 "P1SprBates_MedDocScore", "P2FallRamos_PhysExamScore", "P2FallRamos_CommScore",
                 "P2FallRamos_OralPresScore", "P2FallPayne_PhysExamScore", "P2FallPayne_CommScore",
                 "P2FallPayne_MedDocScore", "P2SpringHyde_PhysExamScore", "P2SpringHyde_CommScore",
                 "P2SpringHyde_MedDocScore","P2SpringSnelling_PhysExamScore", "P2SpringSnelling_CommScore",
                 "P2SpringSnelling_MedDocScore")

#these below excludes any OralPresScore and MedDocScore
final_ordered_osce <- c("P1FallBodySys_PhysExamScore","P1SprBates_PhysExamScore","P1SprBates_CommScore",
                 "P2FallRamos_PhysExamScore", "P2FallRamos_CommScore",
                 "P2FallPayne_PhysExamScore","P2FallPayne_CommScore",
                 "P2SpringHyde_PhysExamScore", "P2SpringHyde_CommScore",
                 "P2SpringSnelling_PhysExamScore", "P2SpringSnelling_CommScore")


df <- df |> 
  mutate(gender = factor(gender, levels = c('M', 'F','D'), labels = c('Male', 'Female', 'unknown')))


df <- df |> 
  mutate(URM = factor(URM, levels = c(0, 1, 3), labels = c('Non-URM', 'URM', 'unknown')))


df <- df |> 
   mutate(URM_AAMC = factor(URM_AAMC, levels = c(0, 1, 3), labels = c('Non-URiM', 'URiM', 'unknown'))) 


df <- df |> mutate(across(ends_with("_Final_Course_Grade"),
                    ~ factor(.x,
                             levels = c(0,1,2,3,9),
                             labels = c('Fail', 'Pass', 'High Pass', 'Honors', 'Pass with remediation')))) 


df <- df |> mutate(across(ends_with("_clinical_grade"),
                   ~ factor(.x, 
                            levels = c(0,1,2,3,9),
                            labels= c('Fail', 'Pass', 'High Pass', 
                                      'Honors', 'Pass with remediation'))))

#Creating relevant tables (clinical clerkship and final clerkship grades, USMLE scores)

clinical_table <- df |> select(ends_with("_clinical_grade"), 'URM')
  
course_grades <- df |> select(all_of(ends_with("_Final_Course_Grade")), 'URM') 

usmle_scores_prep  <- df |> select('STEP1_ExamScore', 'STEP2CK_ExamScore', 'URM')
```

Gender variable: The variable gender for this data set is pretty equal, there is one row that has that variable marked as 'unknown'. N=198 with either male or female

URM variable vs URM_AAMC : The URM variable provides higher overall representation of underrepresented in medicine students within the cohort compared to the stricter criteria (URM_AAMC). I suggest we use the URM variable in analysis for preventing small sample size limitations, maintaining adequate statistical power, and allowing for a more robust comparative evaluation.

```{r, echo=FALSE}

summary(df$URM)

```
```{r, echo=FALSE}
summary(df$URM_AAMC)
```


Clinical vs Final Clerkship grades: Guth during video mentions a wanting to focus on the final clerkship grades. There is a lot of missingness for some final clerkship grades (RRC, AAC) and others have only one option heavily preferred of 'Pass' (EC, MSK)

```{r, echo=FALSE}
tbl_summary(clinical_table)

```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
urm_status_clinical <- clinical_table |>   
  pivot_longer(
    cols = ends_with("_clinical_grade"),
    names_to = "Clinical_Clerkship",
    values_to = "Grade"
  ) |> 
  # Fixed: Use %in% and separate the is.na condition with a comma
  filter(URM %in% c("Non-URM", "URM"), !is.na(Grade)) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = URM, fill = Grade)) +
  geom_bar(position = "dodge", alpha = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ Clinical_Clerkship) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Clinical Clerkship Grades by URM Status",
    x = "URM Status",
    y = "Number of Students",
    fill = "Grade"
  )
```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
# ---- 4. USMLE scores by URM status table----
usmle_tbl <- df %>%
  # Use URM instead of URM_grp, and filter for valid groups
  filter(URM %in% c("Non-URM", "URM")) %>%
  select(URM, STEP1_ExamScore, STEP2CK_ExamScore) %>%
  tbl_summary(
    by = URM,
    label = list(STEP1_ExamScore ~ "USMLE Step 1", STEP2CK_ExamScore ~ "USMLE Step 2 CK"),
    type = all_continuous() ~ "continuous2",
    statistic = all_continuous() ~ c("{mean} ({sd})", "{median} [{p25}, {p75}]"),
    digits = all_continuous() ~ 1,
    missing_text = "Missing"
  ) %>%
   add_overall() #%>%
  # # Kept add_difference (removed add_p to prevent the column collision error)
  # add_difference(test = all_continuous() ~ "t.test") %>%
  # bold_labels()
usmle_tbl
```

OSCE: aggregated osce scores across competency/component (communication or physical exam - these were the ones Guth had the most interest in)

```{r, echo=FALSE}
osce_stat_table <- df |> 
  summarise(across(all_of(final_ordered_osce), 
                   list(
                     Mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     SD   = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     Median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     IQR  = ~IQR(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     Min  = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     Max  = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     N    = ~sum(!is.na(.x))
                   ))) |> 
  # Pivot longer safely by splitting at the *last* underscore
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = c("OSCE_Exam", "Statistic"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(Mean|SD|Median|IQR|Min|Max|N)$"
  ) |> 
  # Pivot wider using the correct 'value' column name generated by pivot_longer
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Statistic,
    values_from = value
  )
osce_stat_table
```


```{r, echo=FALSE}
osce_stat_table_urm <- df |> 
  filter(URM %in% c("Non-URM", "URM")) |> 
  group_by(URM) |> 
  summarise(across(all_of(final_ordered_osce), 
                   list(
                     Mean = ~mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     SD   = ~sd(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     Median = ~median(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     IQR  = ~IQR(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     Min  = ~min(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     Max  = ~max(.x, na.rm = TRUE),
                     N    = ~sum(!is.na(.x))
                   ))) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -URM,
    names_to = c("OSCE_Exam", "Statistic"),
    names_pattern = "^(.*)_(Mean|SD|Median|IQR|Min|Max|N)$"
  ) |> 
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Statistic,
    values_from = value
  )

view(osce_stat_table_urm)
```



```{r, echo=FALSE}
osce_stat_table |> 
ggplot(aes(x = reorder(OSCE_Exam, Mean), y = Mean, fill = OSCE_Exam)) +
  # Draw the bars for the mean score
  geom_col(alpha = 0.8, show.legend = FALSE) +
  # Add error bars representing +/- 1 Standard Deviation
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - SD, ymax = Mean + SD), width = 0.2) +
  # Flip coordinates so exam names are easy to read on the y-axis
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Mean Scores with Standard Deviation by OSCE Exam",
    x = "OSCE Exam",
    y = "Mean Score"
  )
```



```{r, echo=FALSE}
# Summary table grouped by URM and OSCE exams
osce_urm_summary_table <- df |> 
  filter(URM %in% c("Non-URM", "URM")) |>

  summarise(across(all_of(final_ordered_osce),

                   ))) |> 
  pivot_longer(

    values_from = value
  )

# Create the side-by-side grouped bar chart with error bars
osce_urm_summary_table |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(OSCE_Exam, Mean), y = Mean, fill = URM)) +
  # position_dodge places the URM and Non-URM bars side-by-side
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  # Match the error bar position to the dodged bars
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - SD, ymax = Mean + SD), 
                position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.2) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Mean OSCE Scores by URM Status With SD",
    x = "OSCE Exam",
    y = "Mean Score",
    fill = "URM Status"
  )
```


```{r, echo=FALSE}

# I had AI help with this code below. I used Gemini 3 to help me with combining of 
# groups with grepl. I also used grepl documentation to double check other arguments I could use. 
# grepl documentation https://www.rdocumentation.org/packages/base/versions/3.6.2/topics/grep


df_categorized <- df |> 
  filter(URM %in% c("Non-URM", "URM")) |> 
  select(URM, all_of(final_ordered_osce)) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -URM,
    names_to = "Exam_Name",
    values_to = "Score"
  ) |> 
  # Create a grouped category based on keywords in the exam names
  mutate(Competency = case_when(
    grepl("Comm", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Communication Score",
    grepl("Phys|Physical", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Physical Exam Score",
    grepl("Med|Doc", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Medical Documentation",
    grepl("Oral|Pres", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Oral Presentation",
    TRUE ~ "Other" # Catch-all for any remaining exams
  ))


competency_summary <- df_categorized |> 
  group_by(URM, Competency) |> 
  summarise(
    Mean = mean(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD = sd(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(x = reorder(Competency, Mean), y = Mean, fill = URM)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.7, alpha = 0.8) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = Mean - SD, ymax = Mean + SD), 
                position = position_dodge(0.8), width = 0.2) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(
    title = "Aggregated OSCE Competency Scores by URM Status",
    x = "Competency Category",
    y = "Mean Score",
    fill = "URM Status"
  )

competency_summary

```

```{r, echo=FALSE}

competency_stat_table <- df |> 
  filter(URM %in% c("Non-URM", "URM")) |> 
  select(URM, all_of(final_ordered_osce)) |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = -URM,
    names_to = "Exam_Name",
    values_to = "Score"
  ) |> 
  mutate(Competency = case_when(
    grepl("Comm", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Communication Score",
    grepl("Phys|Physical", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Physical Exam Score",
    grepl("Med|Doc", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Medical Documentation",
    grepl("Oral|Pres", Exam_Name, ignore.case = TRUE) ~ "Oral Presentation",
    TRUE ~ "Other"
  )) |> 
  filter(!is.na(Score)) |> 
  group_by(URM, Competency) |> 
  summarise(
    Mean   = mean(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD     = sd(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    Median = median(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    IQR    = IQR(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    Min    = min(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    Max    = max(Score, na.rm = TRUE),
    N      = sum(!is.na(Score)),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |> 
  arrange(Competency, URM)


competency_stat_table


```

```{r, echo=FALSE}
#---Osce missingness table- not grouped-----##
miss_tbl <- df %>%
  select(URM, all_of(final_ordered_osce), STEP1_ExamScore, STEP2CK_ExamScore) %>%
  summarise(across(-URM, list(n_miss = ~sum(is.na(.x)),
                                  pct_miss = ~round(mean(is.na(.x)) * 100, 1)))) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("variable", ".value"),
               names_pattern = "(.*)_(n_miss|pct_miss)") %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = c(final_ordered_osce, "STEP1_ExamScore", "STEP2CK_ExamScore"))) %>%
  arrange(variable)
view(miss_tbl)

```





```{r, echo=FALSE}

#Checking OSCE missingness per cases(rows) to figure out if there's anything weird or that we have to change
# ---- 1. Number of missing OSCE scores per student ----
osce_missing <- df %>%
  mutate(n_osce_miss = rowSums(is.na(across(all_of(final_ordered_osce)))),
         pct_osce_miss = round(n_osce_miss / length(final_ordered_osce) * 100, 1))


all_n_osce_missing <- osce_missing %>% count(n_osce_miss) %>% mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1))

all_n_osce_missing

urm_osce_miss <- osce_missing %>% count(URM, n_osce_miss) %>%
  group_by(URM) %>% mutate(pct = round(n / sum(n) * 100, 1))

urm_osce_miss

# ---- 3. Is missingness related to URM status? ----
osce_missing_stat <- osce_missing %>% filter(URM %in% c("Non-URM", "URM")) %>%
  group_by(URM) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), 
            mean_miss = mean(n_osce_miss), 
            median_miss = median(n_osce_miss),
            pct_any_missing = mean(n_osce_miss > 0) * 100)

osce_missing_stat
```
